title: Reduced components and projective-line descent over algebraically closed fields
statement: Let $k\subseteq L$ be algebraically closed fields [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-pc-field-extension], and let $C$ be a finite type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with no separatedness assumption. For each irreducible component of $C$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], give its closed subset the reduced induced closed-subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], denoting the resulting scheme by $R$. Then $R_L=R\times_kL$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is reduced and irreducible, the projection $R_L\to R$ is surjective, and $R\mapsto R_L$ is a bijection between the reduced component schemes of $C$ and of $C_L$. For each such $R$ one has $R_L\cong\mathbf P^1_L$ over $L$ if and only if $R\cong\mathbf P^1_k$ over $k$, where the projective line is [def-sc-p1-standard, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. More precisely, any $L$-isomorphism between $R_L$ and $\mathbf P^1_L$, together with its inverse, descends to mutually inverse morphisms between $R\times_k\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\mathbf P^1_A$ for some finitely generated $k$-subalgebra $A\subseteq L$. There is a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset A$ with $A/\mathfrak m\cong k$, and specialization of these morphisms gives the asserted $k$-isomorphism. This does not assert that the given $L$-isomorphism itself is defined over $k$. The empty scheme is allowed.

source.place: Tag 038F (lemma-bijection-irreducible-components); limits.tex Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), parts (2)--(3); algebra.tex Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz); returned Steps 9--10.

proof.text: Fix a component $T\subseteq |C|$ and its reduced induced scheme $R$. The reduced-induced-subscheme theorem gives a reduced closed immersion with support $T$; hence $R$ is nonempty and irreducible. On a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ of $C$, its inverse images are $\operatorname{Spec}(B_i/I_i)$, where $I_i$ is radical. Each quotient is a finitely generated $k$-algebra, so these finitely many affines exhibit $R$ as finite type over $k$. The spectrum of a field is locally Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. Thus the local-Noetherian ascent and local-finite-presentation results give that $R$ is locally Noetherian and locally finitely presented over $k$. Its finite-type hypothesis gives quasi-compactness; local Noetherianity gives quasi-separatedness. Its structure morphism is quasi-separated by qcqs morphism permanence. Consequently $R\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite presentation, without requiring $C$ or $R$ separated.

Use $k$ itself as an algebraic closure of $k$. Since $R\times_k k\cong R$ is reduced, the chosen-algebraic-closure test says that $R$ is geometrically reduced. In particular $R_L$ is reduced. Algebraic closedness also implies separable closedness (every irreducible separable polynomial is linear). Apply the subset geometric-irreducibility lemma with $X=R$, subset $|R|$, and $\Omega=k$ with its identity extension. Its initial inverse image is the nonempty irreducible space $|R|$. Its conclusion for $E=L$ says exactly that $R_L$ is nonempty and irreducible.

The projection $R_L\to R$ is surjective. Indeed, on any affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $R$, its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_k L)$ by the affine fibre-product formula. The map $B\to B\otimes_k L$ is faithfully flat by field-extension base change, and hence its map on spectra is surjective. Every point of $R$ belongs to one of these affines.

source.place: algebra.tex Tag 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings), implication (1) to (2); affine field base change.

proof.text: For every field extension $E/k$, the tensor-of-fields lemma over the separably closed field $k$ says that $\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_kE)$ is irreducible and nonempty. The affine fibre-product formula therefore makes $\operatorname{Spec}L$ geometrically irreducible over $k$. Apply the product-component bijection with $U=\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $V=C$. It gives a bijection from the components of $C_L$ to those of $C$, induced by projection. For a component $W$ corresponding to $T$, its image is contained in $T$, so $W$ lies in the full inverse image of $T$. That inverse image is the support of $R_L$: on an affine chart it is $V(I_i(B_i\otimes_kL))$, because $(B_i/I_i)\otimes_kL\cong(B_i\otimes_kL)/I_i(B_i\otimes_kL)$ by the universal property of tensor products. Step 2 makes this support irreducible, so maximality of $W$ gives $W=|R_L|$.

Base change of the closed immersion $R\hookrightarrow C$ is a closed immersion $R_L\hookrightarrow C_L$. Step 2 supplies reducedness, and Step 4 identifies its support with the corresponding component. The uniqueness clause for the reduced induced closed subscheme identifies it with that component's reduced scheme. Conversely every component of $C_L$ occurs in Step 4, and distinct components of $C$ have distinct corresponding supports. These identifications prove the asserted bijection of reduced component schemes.

source.place: schemes.tex Tags 01JY (base change of immersions) and 01J3 (uniqueness of reduced closed subschemes).

proof.text: The standard cover of $P=\mathbf P^1_k=\operatorname{Proj}k[x_0,x_1]$ consists of $\operatorname{Spec}k[t]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k[s]$ with intersection $\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$, where $s=t^{-1}$. The two polynomial algebras are finitely generated; the finite cover makes $P$ finite type and quasi-compact. Each intersection is affine, hence quasi-compact, so the affine-cover criterion makes $P$ quasi-separated. The local-finite-presentation result over the locally Noetherian $\operatorname{Spec}k$, and qcqs morphism permanence, show that $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite presentation. Next, $P$ is the base-change projective line $P'=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};\operatorname{Spec}k)=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$. By the standard-charts lemma with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, (a) and (c), $P'$ is covered by $D_+(T_0)_S=\operatorname{Spec}k[u_{1/0}]$ and $D_+(T_1)_S=\operatorname{Spec}k[u_{0/1}]$. By (b) on the first chart, $T_1=u_{1/0}T_0$ with $T_0$ a free generator, so $D_+(T_1)_S\cap D_+(T_0)_S$ is the locus $D(u_{1/0})=\operatorname{Spec}k[u_{1/0},u_{1/0}^{-1}]$, on which $T_0=u_{0/1}T_1=u_{0/1}u_{1/0}T_0$ gives $u_{0/1}=u_{1/0}^{-1}$. Hence $t\mapsto u_{1/0}$, $s\mapsto u_{0/1}$ define chart isomorphisms over $k$ that agree on the overlaps, and they glue to a $k$-isomorphism $P\cong P'$. By this identification, the base-change definition of projective space and associativity of fibre products, $P\times_k\operatorname{Spec}A\cong\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}=\mathbf P^1_A$ for every $k$-algebra $A$, in particular for $A=L$ and $A=k$.

source.place: morphisms.tex Tag 01TX (lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation); the two standard projective-line charts.

proof.text: Index by the set $I$ of finitely generated $k$-subalgebras $A\subseteq L$, ordered by inclusion. It is nonempty since it contains $k$, and directed since the algebra generated by the union of two finite generating sets contains both. The algebra-union lemma gives $L=\varinjlim_{A\in I}A$. The spectrum-colimit theorem identifies $\operatorname{Spec}L$ with $\varprojlim_{A\in I}\operatorname{Spec}A$ and gives affine transition maps; all stages are qcqs by the affine-scheme theorem. The stage $A=k$ has the two finite-presentation models $R$ and $P$ from Steps 1 and 6. Their pullbacks to later stages remain of finite presentation by base-change permanence.

Suppose $\alpha:R_L\xrightarrow{\sim}P_L$ is the given $L$-isomorphism and write $\beta=\alpha^{-1}$. Apply clause (2) of the spreading-out theorem to $\alpha$ and the fixed models $R,P$ at stage $k$. Apply it again to $\beta$ with the models interchanged. Choose a stage $A_0\subseteq L$ containing the two resulting finitely generated subalgebras, and pull both morphisms to $A_0$. This produces $a:R_{A_0}\to P_{A_0}$ and $b:P_{A_0}\to R_{A_0}$ whose base changes, under the canonical fibre-product identifications, are precisely $\alpha$ and $\beta$. The theorem requires finite presentation and qcqs base stages, verified in Steps 1, 6 and 7; it imposes no separatedness assumption.

The base changes of $b\circ a$ and $\mathrm{id}_{R_{A_0}}$ agree, and so do those of $a\circ b$ and $\mathrm{id}_{P_{A_0}}$, because $\beta\alpha=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha\beta=\mathrm{id}$. Apply clause (3) of spreading out to each pair, and choose one later stage $A\subseteq L$ containing the two equality stages. Base change preserves composition and identities, so the pulled-back maps $a_A,b_A$ satisfy both inverse identities over $A$. They still base change to the prescribed maps $\alpha,\beta$. This proves the stated descent of the isomorphism together with its inverse to a finitely generated $k$-subalgebra, rather than just descent of an abstract isomorphism class.

The algebra $A\subseteq L$ is nontrivial, so the maximal-ideal theorem gives $\mathfrak m\subset A$. The point $\mathfrak m$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is closed, and $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is finite type over $k$ because $A$ is finitely generated. The closed-point residue-field theorem identifies its structural residue map $k\to\kappa(\mathfrak m)=A/\mathfrak m$ with an isomorphism. Thus the quotient followed by its inverse is a $k$-algebra map $A\to k$. Pull back $a_A,b_A$ along this map. Fibre-product associativity identifies their sources and targets with $R$ and $P$, and pulling back their two inverse identities gives mutually inverse $k$-morphisms $R\leftrightarrows\mathbf P^1_k$.

source.place: Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz) and morphisms.tex Tag 01TB (closed-point residue fields).

proof.text: Conversely, a $k$-isomorphism $R\cong\mathbf P^1_k$ and its inverse base change to mutually inverse $L$-morphisms, using $\mathbf P^1_k\times_kL\cong\mathbf P^1_L$. The specialization in Step 10 is allowed to change the chosen $L$-isomorphism: it proves existence of a $k$-isomorphism and does not claim that $\alpha$ is defined over $k$. If $C$ is empty, it has no irreducible components and neither does its base change; the component correspondence is the empty bijection, and all assertions quantified over $R$ are vacuous.
